title: Volumes, bind mounts and tmpfs
summary: Containers are disposable, data is not. Three ways to put data outside the writable layer.

steps.title: The writable layer is disposable
body: Everything a container writes goes into its thin **writable layer** on top of the read-only image layers. That layer is deleted with the container.
│ writable layer            │  ✗ gone: your Postgres tables were here

That is a feature: you can throw containers away and recreate them from the image at any time (upgrades, crashes, scaling). But it means **anything worth keeping must live outside the container**, in a mount.

steps.prompt: You run Postgres with `docker run -d --name db postgres:17`, create tables, then `docker rm -f db` and start it again with the same command. What do you find?
options: An empty database: the data lived in the old container's writable layer
The same tables, because Docker keeps a container's data per image
The same tables, because the container name is the same
An error: the image is now corrupted
steps.explain: Nothing ties the new container to the old one's writable layer. Mount a volume at Postgres's data directory to keep the data.

steps.title: Three kinds of mount
body: tmpfs           RAM only, never written to disk ◀───▶  /tmp
| **named volume** | `-v pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data` | databases and anything the app must keep; survives `docker rm`, easy to back up, fast on every OS |
| **bind mount** | `-v ./src:/app/src` (or an absolute path) | development: edit code on the host, see it live in the container; also mounting a single config file |
| **tmpfs** | `--tmpfs /tmp` | scratch or sensitive files that must never touch disk; gone when the container stops |

The `-v` rule: if the part before `:` is a **path** (starts with `/`, `.` or `~`), it is a bind mount; otherwise it is a volume **name**. `-v /data` alone (no colon) creates an **anonymous** volume with a random name. Add `:ro` to make a mount read-only.
The long form says the same thing explicitly: `--mount type=volume,source=pgdata,target=/var/lib/postgresql/data`.

steps.prompt: Which kind of mount fits best?
items: Live-reloading your source code while developing
A decrypted key that must never be written to disk
Uploaded files the app must keep across upgrades
Mounting one `nginx.conf` from your repo, read-only
A cache that can be thrown away on every restart

pairs: a read-only bind mount of a host folder
a bind mount of an absolute host path

steps.prompt: Two containers, one after the other, share a named volume. What does the second command print?
code: docker run --rm -v notes:/data alpine sh -c "echo remember > /data/todo.txt"
steps.explain: The first container is deleted (`--rm`), but the file lives in the `notes` volume, which the second container mounts.

steps.prompt: A Node app works when built, but when you add `-v .:/app` for development it fails with `Cannot find module 'express'`. Why?
options: The bind mount hides the image's `/app`, including the `node_modules` that `npm ci` installed at build time
Bind mounts are read-only by default
Node cannot read files from a Windows host
Named volumes and bind mounts cannot be combined
steps.explain: A mount replaces whatever the image had at that path. A common fix is an extra anonymous volume for `/app/node_modules`, so the image's copy shows through, or installing on the host too.

steps.prompt: Keep Postgres data in a named volume and a read-only init script from the repo.
steps.explain: `pgdata` (no slash) is a volume name. `./init.sql` starts with `.`, so it is a bind mount of a host file. `init.sql` without `./` would be treated as a volume *name*.

steps.title: Classify a -v value
prompt: Write `string ClassifyMount(string spec)` for a `-v` value (Linux-style paths only):
1. Split on `:`. If there are at least two parts and the last is `ro` or `rw`, remove it; `ro` makes the mount read-only.
3. Otherwise SOURCE is the first part and TARGET the second. A SOURCE starting with `/`, `.` or `~` gives `bind mount SOURCE -> TARGET`; any other gives `named volume SOURCE -> TARGET`.
template: Dojo.Eq("a file name without ./ is a volume name", "named volume init.sql -> /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/init.sql", ClassifyMount("init.sql:/docker-entrypoint-initdb.d/init.sql"));
hints: Turn the split into a `List<string>` so you can remove the `ro`/`rw` suffix.
Decide bind versus named only by the first character of SOURCE.
